introduction-the-reference-implementatio.core: AWS is the reference implementation of cloud computing. Most cloud concepts (regions, availability zones, IAM, VPCs, object storage) were popularised by AWS, and other clouds map onto them. Learning AWS's physical and logical layout gives you a mental model that transfers across providers.

first_principles.problem: Engineers learn services in isolation and can't reason about where things physically run or how failures spread.
truths: Cloud resources live in physical buildings.

analogy.title: A global franchise with a standard operating manual
analogy.story: Every branch follows the same blueprint, so learning one teaches you all.
analogy.breaks: Franchises are identical; AWS regions differ in services and prices.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: You know what an AZ outage affects.

check.q: Is an EBS volume global, regional or zonal?
check.a: Zonal: it lives in a single availability zone.

the-hierarchy-regions-vs-azs-vs-data-cen.core: A region is a geographic area containing multiple availability zones (typically 3+). Each AZ is one or more data centres with independent power, cooling and networking, tens of kilometres apart and linked by low-latency fibre. Spreading across AZs survives data-centre failures; spreading across regions survives regional disasters.

first_principles.problem: An app in a single AZ goes down when that facility loses power.
truths: Distance reduces correlated failure but adds latency.
derivation: Consider **multi-region** for DR or global users.
Remember AZ names are **mapped per account** (use AZ IDs).

analogy.title: A bank with branches in different neighbourhoods of one city
analogy.story: A fire in one branch doesn't stop the others; a citywide disaster needs a branch in another city.
analogy.breaks: Branches are independent businesses; AZs are tightly networked for synchronous replication.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Losing one AZ keeps two-thirds of capacity.

code.text:
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name web \
  --vpc-zone-identifier subnet-a,subnet-b,subnet-c --min-size 3 --max-size 9 \
  --launch-template LaunchTemplateName=web

check.q: Why do AZ names like us-east-1a differ between accounts?
check.a: AWS maps names to physical AZs per account to spread load; use AZ IDs (use1-az1) to align across accounts.

the-edge-network-bringing-content-closer.core: AWS runs hundreds of edge locations (points of presence) worldwide, far more than regions. CloudFront caches content there, Route 53 answers DNS there, and Global Accelerator brings user traffic onto the AWS backbone close to the user, reducing latency and absorbing DDoS attacks.

first_principles.problem: Users in Sydney wait 300 ms per request to an origin in Virginia.
truths: The speed of light limits latency.
Caching near users avoids long trips.
The AWS backbone is faster than the public internet.
derivation: **Cache** static and cacheable content at the edge (CloudFront).
**Run logic** at the edge (CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge).

analogy.title: Local convenience stores supplied by a central warehouse
analogy.story: Popular items are stocked nearby; rare ones are fetched from the warehouse.
analogy.breaks: Stores sell physical stock; edge caches can serve the same object to millions at once.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Faster for users, cheaper for you.

check.q: What's the difference between a region and an edge location?
check.a: Regions host full services and data; edge locations cache content and handle DNS, CDN and network entry close to users.

special-zones-local-zones-wavelength.core: Local Zones extend a region into a metro area (e.g. Los Angeles) for single-digit-ms latency to nearby users with a subset of services (EC2, EBS, some databases). Wavelength Zones embed AWS compute inside telecom 5G networks for ultra-low-latency mobile apps. Both are anchored to a parent region.

first_principles.problem: A video-editing or gaming app needs < 10 ms latency to users far from any region.
truths: Not every city has a region.
5G traffic traverses carrier networks before reaching the internet.
derivation: Keep **control and data** stores in the parent region where possible.

analogy.title: A satellite branch office
analogy.story: Close to local clients for quick meetings, but headquarters still handles most functions.
analogy.breaks: Satellite offices can grow into HQs; Local Zones stay limited extensions.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Subnets in LA serve Hollywood studios at ~2 ms.

check.q: What's the main limitation of Local Zones?
check.a: They offer only a subset of AWS services and depend on a parent region.

partitions-the-hard-boundaries.core: A partition is a completely separate AWS instance: aws (commercial), aws-cn (China, operated by local partners) and aws-us-gov (GovCloud). Accounts, IAM, credentials and APIs don't cross partitions, and ARNs include the partition, so code must not hard-code arn:aws:.

first_principles.problem: A tool fails in GovCloud because it hard-codes 'arn:aws:' and commercial endpoints.
truths: Partitions are isolated legal and technical domains.
derivation: Maintain **separate accounts and credentials** per partition.

analogy.title: Separate countries with separate passports
analogy.story: Your passport from one doesn't work in the other's systems.
analogy.breaks: Countries have treaties; partitions have no identity federation between them.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Template works in commercial, China and GovCloud.

check.q: Can an IAM role in the commercial partition be assumed from GovCloud?
check.a: No: identities and trust don't cross partitions.
